title: Fourth Geneva Convention
summary: The Geneva Convention relative to the protection of civilian persons in time of war was concluded at Geneva on 12 August 1949, with Switzerland as depositary. It entered into force on 21 October 1950 and was later joined by many states. It is one of four 1949 Geneva Conventions, though it gives civilians no protection from the conduct of hostilities.

importance.justification: Core treaty of international humanitarian law protecting civilians in war, with near-universal participation.
